decisions.reason: It is very close to the firm's core dental practice software and benefits from the firm's in-house R&D, so management is likely to keep improving it rather than withdraw it.
Although less central than software, it builds on the firm's existing training, customer relationships, and dental domain knowledge, which makes continued learning and adaptation feasible.
A remote support tool is closely connected to the firm's established support and software activities, so it fits existing capabilities and is likely to remain useful to customers.
Analytics directly extend the value of the firm's installed software base and align with its direction toward more digital and efficiently managed practices.
A complete practice bundle is highly complementary to the firm's broad established offer and should be easy for management to refine and commercialize with existing knowledge.
A job and practice listing portal is relatively distant from the firm's core software knowledge, so even with in-house R&D management is less able to interpret results and improve it confidently.
